title: Computation normalization of the canonical balanced scalar tensor presentation
statement: Let $a:R\to S$ be a morphism of commutative condensed rings [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]. For every scheme $T$ use ordinary internal-module derived categories [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Write $D_T$ for derived extension, $V_T$ for exact restriction, $B_T=V_TS_T[0]$, and $\operatorname{TensorNormalized}$ for the computation-counit equation of [def-sfb-internal-derived-scalar-comparisons]. Define $t_T$ by the ordinary balanced extension/restriction isomorphism followed by symmetry, and by the fixed derived isomorphism $\operatorname{residueDerivedTensorIso}$ of [new-integral-residue-tensor-presentation]. Then $\operatorname{TensorNormalized}(t_T)$ for every $T$. Moreover, for every scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$, the exact-single restricted-regular pullback isomorphism $\operatorname{regularPullback}(a,f)$ of [def-sfb-restricted-regular-pullback-data] equals $\operatorname{residueRestrictedRegularPullIso}(R,S,a,f)$ of [def-weil-pbc-integral-residue-tensor-pull-presentation], after exposing their identical total derived pullback and degree-zero endpoints. No exactness of scalar extension is assumed.

proof.text: Apply derivedTensorPresentationIso_fac from [new-integral-residue-tensor-presentation] to the homotopy quotient of a cochain complex. The single/quotient comparison is the composite of two identity maps. Postcompose with the quotient of the Koszul braiding and the second single-tensor comparison; braidedness of Qh cancels the derived inverse braiding. The first and second single-tensor comparisons identify the resulting map with the termwise ordinary braiding: expand the bicomplex braiding, cancel the total flip, and use ordinary braiding naturality and the inverse/hom identity of the first single comparison. Expand the balanced counit and restriction localization factor at the generic module-category level. Functoriality of Q and mapHomologicalComplex gives the ordinary balanced comparison followed by braiding. Specialize to coefficientMap(a,T) and remove the identity quotient factors in compute of [def-sfb-internal-derived-scalar-comparisons]. This proves TensorNormalized for every complex, without a flatness assumption.

proof.text: Compare the ordinary unit maps of the standard composite monoidal pullback and the transported structure of [new-integral-residue-ordinary-monoidal]. The standard formula is scalar extension applied to mapMod's identity unit morphism, followed by the scalar-extension inverse unit; functoriality removes the mapped identity, after which its formula is definitionally the transported formula. Hence the ordinary restricted-regular comparisons agree. Expand singleFunctorCompLeftDerivedFunctorIso and use the exact mapDerivedCategory single-object comparison formula. Both sides have the same exact localization factor, single-complex comparison and ordinary restricted-regular map; Q.map_comp identifies their last factors. This gives the equality with [def-weil-pbc-integral-residue-tensor-pull-presentation].

lean.statement:
theorem canonicalCoefficientTensorNormalization_normalized :
    (∀ T : Scheme.{u},
      TensorNormalized a T (canonicalCoefficientTensorNormalization a T)) ∧
    (∀ {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y),
      RestrictedCoefficientMate.regularPullback a f =
      (by
        unfold L CondensedRing.moduleObjectDerivedPullback
        let e := CondensedRing.residueRestrictedRegularPullIso R S a f
        unfold CondensedRing.residueExchangeUpperStar at e
        run_tac Lean.Elab.Tactic.withMainContext do
          let e ← Lean.Meta.getLocalDeclFromUserName `e
          (← Lean.Elab.Tactic.getMainGoal).assign e.toExpr
          Lean.Elab.Tactic.replaceMainGoal []))
